The problematic code segment installs the `lito` binary by piping an unverified script from GitHub into `bash`. Even though the domain (github.com) is legitimate, the script fetches from the mutable `main` branch, meaning the content can change at any time without notice or audit trail. An attacker who compromises the repository or gains write access could inject malicious commands that would be silently executed during the build process, potentially leading to data exfiltration, backdoor installation, or system compromise.

This behavior constitutes a genuine security threat because it executes unsigned, unreviewed, remotely fetched code as part of the build pipeline — a classic vector for supply-chain attacks.
